desc:
A chess knight stands on the square (sr, sc) of an n x n board (rows and columns are numbered from 0). One knight move changes the position by (±1, ±2) or (±2, ±1), and the knight may never leave the board. Other pieces are not present.

Return the minimum number of moves needed to reach (tr, tc), or -1 if the target is unreachable. If the knight already stands on the target, the answer is 0.

n = 8, start = (0,0), target = (7,7)  ->  6
n = 3, start = (0,0), target = (1,1)  -> -1     (the centre of a 3x3 board is never reachable)
hints: Think of the squares as nodes and legal knight moves as edges. All edges cost one move.
Run BFS from the start square, generating the eight knight moves and discarding those outside the board.
Small boards are the tricky cases: on 1x1, 2x2 and 3x3 boards some squares cannot be reached at all, so the search simply ends without finding the target and the answer is -1.
editorial: The knight graph on an n × n board is unweighted, so BFS from the start gives the minimum number of moves to every square. Generate the eight offsets (1,2),(2,1),(-1,2),..., keep those inside the board, and store a distance for every square.

There is no formula to rely on for bounded boards: near corners and edges the knight loses moves, and the tiny boards are not connected (on 3 × 3 the centre has no moves in or out; on 2 × 2 the knight cannot move at all). BFS handles all of that automatically and returns -1 when the target is never found.
There are n² squares with eight neighbours each, so the work is O(n²) time and memory.
